title: Six Thinking Hats
author: Edward de Bono
edition_analyzed: Second edition, reprinted with updates (most commonly referenced edition)
target_audience: Teams seeking to improve decision-making and collaboration
Students of psychology and organizational behavior
Anyone interested in structured thinking and innovation
primary_purpose: To introduce a simple, systematic framework—using metaphorical 'hats'—that helps individuals and groups approach problems and decisions from multiple perspectives, thereby improving creativity, communication, and effectiveness.

structure_format.organization: Chapters organized by 'hat' color and their associated modes of thinking, followed by practical applications and case studies
features: Descriptions and rationale for each of the six hats
Instructions for applying the method in meetings and personal thinking

key_concepts_lessons: Each 'thinking hat' represents a distinct perspective or mode of thinking: White (facts, information), Red (feelings, intuition), Black (caution, risks), Yellow (optimism, benefits), Green (creativity, alternatives), Blue (process control, organization).
By deliberately adopting each hat, teams avoid habitual arguments and consider all aspects of a problem.
The method encourages organized, parallel thinking rather than adversarial debate.
The hats can be used in sequence to structure meetings or solve problems, ensuring balanced consideration.
Applying the Six Hats technique can reduce meeting time, improve decision quality, and boost creativity.
notable_features: Widely used in business, education, and innovation contexts
Six-color metaphor is memorable and easy to teach
Explicit step-wise instructions for group and solo use
Focus on reducing unproductive conflict and promoting constructive discussion
cultural_historical_context: Developed during a surge of interest in creative thinking and team-based problem solving in the 1980s, De Bono’s approach responded to the limitations of traditional argument-based discussion in organizations.
reception_impact: Adopted globally by corporations, schools, and consultants
Praised for clarity and usefulness in facilitating productive meetings
Critics note it may oversimplify complex discussions or feel artificial if applied rigidly
Significant influence on creative facilitation, education, and organizational change
comparable_titles: Lateral Thinking by Edward de Bono
The Art of Thinking Clearly by Rolf Dobelli
Decision Making and Problem Solving by John Adair
